The remote-meeting question decides whether residents can attend or comment on board meetings from home, and no position has been settled.
watch_next: January 10 meeting: revised ARPA/CLFRF distribution policy, after members send feedback to the town manager by about January 4.
A future agenda item on the open meeting law remote-meeting position.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted 4-1 to approve a package store license and a restaurant all-alcohol license; a second restaurant license passed unanimously.
Common victualler and 2023 miscellaneous license renewals passed unanimously, and the board agreed to discuss making a certificate of good standing an explicit licensing policy.
The board reviewed the remote work policy and the appointment policy line by line; the remote work policy returns next week after minor changes.
The board appointed three members to the new 300th Anniversary Committee and waived first refusal on a Chapter 61 parcel, both unanimously.
The town manager reported on the Lufa Farms project, whose tax increment financing agreement would need a vote at annual town meeting.

why_it_matters: A tax increment financing agreement for Lufa Farms would change how new tax revenue from the project is treated, and residents would be asked to vote on it at annual town meeting.
The remote work and appointment policies set how town staff and volunteer board members are chosen and employed, and the appointment policy is likely to be approved next week.
watch_next: The Select Board meeting on Dec 20, 2022, where the remote work policy returns, the appointment policy is likely to be approved, and the ARPA discussion is scheduled.
The annual town meeting vote on any Lufa Farms tax increment financing agreement.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The records agree on the main licence votes (entertainment and alcohol), the budget figures and the ARPA postponement. Several results and items differ. The official minutes record no result for the Planning Board appointment, the miscellaneous licences or the auto dealer licences, and ours records none for the common victualler vote. Ours also holds decisions (the historic district window application, the JK Waterfront hold) and figures (the $800,000 and $80,000 items) that the official minutes lack.

what_happened.line: The Select Board jointly appointed Tim Wilsmer to the planning board until the next town election, passing unanimously.
The board approved 2023 weekday entertainment, miscellaneous and auto dealer licenses, and renewed alcohol licenses as presented, omitting JK Waterfront.
The JK Waterfront (On the Rocks) alcohol license was held to next week for clarification on a police incident.
The finance director gave a first-quarter FY23 update on local receipts, the tax levy, state aid received and spending through September 30.
The ARPA funding criteria discussion, which touched on ordering the replacement ambulance early, was postponed to next week.

why_it_matters: The ARPA criteria and the ambulance purchase timing are deferred, so how the town's remaining federal relief money is spent has not yet been decided.
One restaurant's alcohol license is not yet renewed for 2023, while the other licenses residents and local businesses rely on were renewed.
watch_next: The ARPA funding criteria discussion and the JK Waterfront license decision, both set for the next week's meeting.
The December 20th meeting, to which the board plans to invite the historic district commission about what makes a window application complete.
